hero.lead: A nation of 118.4 million along the Nile, where every home cooks with clean fuel and the IMF and World Bank are backing reform with more than $8 billion.

capital.heading: Egypt has steadied its economy with the IMF and the World Bank behind it. Next, every child reading by ten.

record.text: Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility: Drawn to date; about $1.77 billion made available in July 2026
GROWTH II Development Policy Financing: Includes a $200 million credit guarantee from the United Kingdom
Support for sustainable, diversified and resilient growth: Budget support for reforms
EU macro-financial assistance: EUR 1 billion disbursed in December 2024, and EUR 2.5 billion of a further EUR 4 billion disbursed in January and July 2026
Sovereign bonds in 2026: a $1 billion 8-year Social Eurobond in May, five times oversubscribed, and a $500 million Samurai bond in June

register.name: Samurai bond
register.detail: Issued June 2026 · yen market
register.note: Sovereign borrowing in Japan
register.text: A sovereign bond sold to investors in Japan, widening the base of lenders behind the public budget that carries the seven standards.

register.name: Social Eurobond, 8 years
register.detail: Issued May 2026 · five times oversubscribed
register.note: A sovereign social bond
register.text: An eight-year social bond sold to international investors, with orders five times the amount raised. A social bond ties borrowing to spending on social outcomes such as health and education.

register.name: GROWTH II Development Policy Financing
register.detail: Approved May 2026 · Budget support
register.note: Includes a $200 million credit guarantee from the United Kingdom
register.text: Backs reforms for quality jobs, sounder public finances and a greener growth model.

register.name: Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.detail: Seventh review completed 30 July 2026 · EFF extended through 15 December 2026
register.note: Drawn to date; about $1.77 billion made available in July 2026
register.text: Inflation eased to 14.3 percent in June 2026, from 15.2 percent in March. The end-September 2026 targets are to be assessed at the eighth review, before the arrangement ends in December 2026.

register.name: Support for sustainable, diversified and resilient growth
register.detail: Approved June 2024 · Development policy financing
register.note: Budget support for reforms
register.text: The first operation in the series that GROWTH II continues.

register.name: Private Sector Development and Economic Diversification Support Programme, Phase II
register.detail: Approved 27 November 2024 · signed 19 January 2026 · budget support for 2024–2025
register.note: Business climate, green growth and formal enterprise
register.text: Budget support to improve the business climate in manufacturing and agribusiness, expand renewable energy, attract private investment and jobs for women and young people, and help informal businesses register. It is aimed at the livelihood, food and energy standards.

register.name: ITFC annual work programme 2025
register.detail: Signed 4 February 2025 · $800 million for EGPC · $700 million for GASC · ICD $100 million for private firms
register.note: Planned trade finance for fuel and strategic food imports
register.text: Islamic trade finance for the state petroleum company and the state commodities buyer, to import fuel and strategic food commodities. It keeps the food and energy standards supplied.
by: Islamic Corporation for the Development of the Private Sector

register.name: Generating Resilience, Opportunities and Welfare for a Thriving Egypt
register.detail: Approved 12 December 2024 · sovereign policy-based financing · first of three for 2025–2028
register.note: Climate policy-based financing
register.text: Policy-based financing for competition and the business climate, revenue mobilisation and debt reduction, and the green transition, with technical support from the World Bank. It is aimed at the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: EU macro-financial assistance, second operation
register.detail: Adopted 24 June 2025 · EUR 1 billion disbursed January 2026 · EUR 1.5 billion disbursed July 2026
register.note: EUR 2.5 billion disbursed by July 2026
register.text: A European Union loan of EUR 4 billion; its first two instalments, EUR 2.5 billion in all, were disbursed in January and July 2026. Macro-financial assistance steadies the public finances that pay for the seven standards.

register.name: EU macro-financial assistance, first operation
register.detail: Disbursed 27 December 2024 · single instalment
register.note: Short-term operation
register.text: A short-term European Union loan of EUR 1 billion, disbursed in a single instalment on 27 December 2024, ahead of the second operation of EUR 4 billion.

register.name: Ras El-Hekma investment deal
register.detail: 2024 · investment from an Abu Dhabi-based investment and holding company
register.note: Reported by the IMF, March 2024
register.text: An investment deal for the development of Ras El-Hekma on the Mediterranean coast. The IMF reports that a large share was committed to raising reserves, clearing foreign currency backlogs and paying down government debt.

register.name: Banque du Caire, initial public offering
register.detail: 2 November 2026 · IFC $100 million · EBRD $100 million · IFC stake about 7%
register.note: Part of the Asset Monetization Program
register.text: Equity in the bank’s initial public offering, to strengthen its capacity to finance businesses and households; the bank expects to grow from about 899,000 to 1.9 million financed customers by 2030. It is aimed at the livelihood standard.

register.name: Dandara solar and battery project, phase 1
register.detail: 28 October 2026 · non-recourse financing · 569 MW solar and 100 MWh battery · operation targeted for the first half of 2028
register.note: EBRD, AfDB and EIB · power for Egypt Aluminium under a 25-year agreement
register.text: Project finance for Scatec’s first phase at Dandara, about 80% of its estimated $271 million cost. It supplies clean power to Egypt Aluminium under a 25-year agreement backed by a sovereign guarantee, for the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Breadfast, equity
register.detail: Approved 23 December 2025 · signed 5 February 2026 · invested 26 February 2026
register.note: Up to $13 million
register.text: Equity in a leading online grocery and quick-commerce brand in Egypt. Faster, wider grocery delivery shortens the chain from farm to table, for the food standard.

register.name: Banque Misr, green and small-business finance
register.detail: Signed 15 February 2026 · 20% of lending for women-owned businesses
register.note: Energy efficiency, sustainable transport, green buildings and renewable energy
register.text: An IFC investment that scales up Banque Misr’s green lending and its finance for micro, small and medium enterprises. It is aimed at the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: GlobalCorp, leasing and factoring for small businesses
register.detail: Signed 15 February 2026 · dual-currency investment · IFC’s first local-currency securitisation in Egypt
register.note: Leasing and factoring for MSMEs
register.text: An IFC investment that widens leasing and factoring for micro, small and medium enterprises and deepens Egypt’s capital market. It is aimed at the livelihood standard.

register.name: GMED Holding, medical products and equipment
register.detail: Signed 15 February 2026
register.note: Production capacity for medical supplies
register.text: An IFC investment to increase the production and supply of medical products and equipment, to expand access to quality healthcare. It is aimed at the health standard.

register.name: Obelisk solar and battery project
register.detail: Financial close 15 June 2025 · 1,125 MW solar · 100 MW / 200 MWh battery · Nagaa Hammadi
register.note: EBRD up to $173.5m, AfDB $184.1m, BII $100m loan and $15m returnable grant
register.text: Non-recourse debt for Scatec’s hybrid solar and storage plant, about 80% of its estimated $590 million cost, with both phases scheduled for 2026. Solar power stored for the evening peak carries the energy standard into the night.

register.name: Abydos battery storage
register.detail: 15 June 2025 · 300 MWh battery at a 500 MWac solar plant in Kom Ombo, Aswan
register.note: With FMO and blended concessional funds
register.text: IFC debt for Egypt’s first utility-scale battery energy storage system, built by AMEA Power beside a solar plant in operation since November 2024. Storage lets daytime sun serve the evening, for the energy standard.

register.name: Suez Wind Farm, 1.1 GW
register.detail: Financial close 2 January 2025 · 138 turbines in two phases of 550 MW · full operation expected by the second quarter of 2027
register.note: Senior debt for a $1.2 billion project by ACWA Power and Hau Energy
register.text: Senior debt from the EBRD, the AfDB, BII, DEG, the OPEC Fund and APICORP for a wind farm on the Gulf of Suez. It adds 1.1 GW of clean electricity to the national grid, for the energy standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 43 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A busy Cairo street at golden hour

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Green irrigated fields along the Nile valley in Upper Egypt, desert beyond

items.name: The Cities
items.label: Live in towns and cities
items.text: Dense cities make every pipe, cable and clinic serve more people for each dollar spent.
items.alt: The modern Cairo skyline along the Nile at dusk

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Below the scarcity line of 1,000 cubic metres: every drop must be stored, treated and reused.
items.alt: The Nile at Aswan with white-sailed feluccas

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of electricity from renewables, 2023
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: The Benban solar park in the desert near Aswan, Egypt, rows of panels to the horizon

items.name: Breadfast
items.text: A leading online grocery and quick-commerce brand in Egypt; IFC invested up to $13 million in equity in February 2026.

items.name: AMEA Power
items.text: Runs a 500 MWac solar plant at Kom Ombo, Aswan, in operation since November 2024, with Egypt’s first utility-scale battery of 300 MWh beside it.

items.name: Nahdet Misr
items.text: A publisher founded in 1938 that has worked with the Ministry of Education since 2018 to develop the new school curricula, and has produced supplementary K-12 books for it since 1968.

items.name: GMED Holding (EGMED)
items.text: Produces and supplies medical products and equipment; IFC signed a $15 million investment in February 2026 to expand its capacity.

items.name: GlobalCorp
items.text: Leasing and factoring for micro, small and medium enterprises; IFC signed a $30 million dual-currency investment in February 2026.

coverage.gap_text: Of Egyptian children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school in 2021.

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
